correctness.rationale: For the finite hard progression n=18k+3, 2<=k<=55,555,555, the embedded C++ `verify.cpp` enumerates all even Zumkeller z<=4288 with descending exact subset-sum DP on complete proper-divisor lists (972 z), constructs complete odd prime Eratosthenes bit sieve <=10^9, and scans all 55,555,554 n, stopping at smallest successful even offset each time. I independently wrote a different C++ sieve/subset-sum enumeration and executed the ENTIRE finite domain, not a sample: checked=55,555,554, uncovered=0, even_z=972, max minimal even offset=4288, unique n=679570815, n-z=679566527 sieve-prime; partial H(X) 464,928,2368,2368 for 10^5 through 10^8. The witness z=4288=64*67 is Zumkeller by sigma(z)=8636 and balanced subset 4288+2+4+8+16=4318. An odd Zumkeller offset for odd n leaves even prime 2 and equals n-2, which cannot improve h(n*) or tie max elsewhere below 4288. Somu–Kukla–Tran Proposition 4.12 covers other congruence classes, yielding full odd 9..10^9 except21. Scope strictly finite; no unbounded conjecture proven.
